researcher_notes: COMPANY CONFIRMED REAL. HQ address printed on every official tear sheet: 425 Waverley Oaks Road, Waltham, MA 02452, USA (phone (617) 444-9263, team@vecnarobotics.com). Country = United States. FOUNDING VERIFIED: Vecna Robotics, Inc. was incorporated in 2018 as a spin-off from parent company Vecna Technologies (itself founded 1998 by MIT alumnus Daniel Theobald); founders of the spin-off are Daniel Theobald and Dan Patt, ~60 employees transferred at spin-out, reincorporated in Delaware, first outside round $13.5M led by Drive Capital (Aug 2018). CEO is Karl Iagnemma. Source: Wikipedia (secondary, citing SEC filing and trade press) -- treat founding details as MEDIUM confidence; the HQ address is independently HIGH because it is printed on Vecna's own tear sheets and About page. Product lineup verified from the company's own page-sitemap.xml -> exactly four vehicle product pages exist: AFL (Autonomous Forklift), ATG (Autonomous Tugger), APT (Autonomous Pallet Truck), CPJ (Co-bot Pallet Jack). All four are genuine load/pallet-transport vehicles and all four are in scope. Vecna also sells 'Pivotal' (orchestration software / Command Center) and 'CaseFlow' (a case-picking solution powered by the CPJ) -- these are software/solution offerings, NOT vehicles, and are deliberately excluded. PRIMARY SOURCES: official 'tear sheet' PDFs linked from each product page, three of which are dated 2026/03 (AFL, ATG, CPJ) and carry both IMPERIAL and METRIC columns -- so all metric values below are the manufacturer's OWN printed metric figures, not my conversions, except where noted. The APT tear sheet is older (uploaded 2022/09, filename 'Workhorse'), so APT data is one generation behind the others. NOTABLE HIGH-VALUE FIND: all four tear sheets explicitly print 'ISO 13849-1:2015 PL=d-rated safety system' -- a published Performance Level, which is rare (most vendors only say 'complies with ISO 13849-1'). functional_safety_level=PLd is therefore HIGH confidence, not inferred. AP0 HINT DEFECT FOUND (see flags in ATG product below): the AP0 hint for turning_radius cites 'Vecna ATG approx 2,900 mm / 9'6"' as an example of TRACTOR-ALONE turning radius. Vecna's own tear sheet qualifies that number as 'TURNING RADIUS (w/ 3 quadsteer carts)' -- i.e. it is a TRAIN turning radius measured with three carts attached, not the tractor alone. The number itself is correct; its attribution in the AP0 hint is wrong. Recommend the hint's example be corrected or removed. VDA 5050: NOT claimed anywhere on Vecna's site or tear sheets -- omitted on all products, never assumed. ISO 3691-4: NOT claimed (US-market vendor, declares ANSI/ITSDF B56.5 + RIA 15.08) -- only ANSI/ITSDF B56.5 recorded. RIA 15.08 is confirmed on all four but has no AP0 allowed value, so it is not recorded. UNIT/SEMANTIC DECISION on min_aisle_width (affects KO_IF_GT): the AFL and APT tear sheets publish TWO different aisle numbers -- a 'RIGHT ANGLE STACK' figure and a 'MINIMUM AISLE WIDTH AT MAX SPEED' figure. The AP0 hint defines min_aisle_width as the 'min WORKING aisle width', which for a fork truck is the right-angle-stack aisle (Ast), not a transit corridor. I therefore recorded the RIGHT ANGLE STACK value as min_aisle_width and documented the smaller travel-aisle figure in each product's notes. Using the smaller number would wrongly qualify these trucks for tight-aisle tenders they cannot actually work in. For the ATG (tugger, no stacking) and CPJ (pallet jack, no stacking) the published aisle figure IS the working aisle, so it was used directly. Fields left out entirely because no source states them: operating temperature/humidity, IP rating, cleanroom class, outdoor capability, gradient, floor flatness, stop/drop/pick accuracy, max fleet size, omnidirectional movement, obstacle bypass, multi-load compatibility, station applications, industries served. PRODUCT-COMPLETENESS CHECK (finalization pass): Wikipedia's infobox lists a fifth product, 'Tote Retrieval System (TRS)', described there as an AGV doing 'mobile piece-picking from conventional shelves'. TRS is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED for two independent reasons: (1) it does not exist anywhere on Vecna's current website -- no product page in page-sitemap.xml, no mention on the 'Our Fleet' page -- so it is not a currently-sold product; (2) even if sold, piece-picking from shelves is not pallet/load transport and is out of the requested category. Wikipedia's product list is demonstrably STALE: it also omits the CPJ entirely, which has been sold since 2022. The authoritative product list is the company's own sitemap, which contains exactly four vehicle pages -- AFL, ATG, APT, CPJ -- all four of which are captured here. No fifth current vehicle exists. Also noted: the CPJ was developed in partnership with forklift manufacturer Big Joe (announced 2022). FLEET-WIDE FIELDS APPLIED IN FINALIZATION: autonomous_obstacle_bypass=true and fleet_control_architecture=Centralized were added to all four products from platform-level sources; navigation_type=Natural Feature (SLAM) was confirmed rather than inferred; vda5050_compatible confirmed ABSENT (zero 'VDA'/'5050' hits across all seven sources) and therefore left unset on every product. PLAUSIBILITY FLAG ON max_speed (read before using it for scoring): the AFL and APT are recorded at 3.0 m/s and the ATG at 2.0 m/s because those are the manufacturer's own printed metric figures. However, 3.0 m/s (6.7 mph) is well above the <=1.5 m/s that is customary for vehicles sharing aisles with pedestrians under the European ISO 3691-4 regime. These are US-market trucks certified to ANSI/ITSDF B56.5, where higher rated speeds are normal, and the AFL sheet itself qualifies its aisle spec as 'MINIMUM AISLE WIDTH AT MAX SPEED' -- implying full speed is only used in wider, cleared corridors and that the truck derates elsewhere. So these are unloaded/rated top speeds, NOT the speed sustained in mixed pedestrian traffic. Since max_speed is a scoring field, this will score Vecna favourably against EU vendors that publish conservative derated speeds; that is an apples-to-oranges comparison worth being aware of. No safety-derated figure is published, so nothing was substituted. ALL OTHER PLAUSIBILITY CHECKS PASS: dimensions, payloads and aisles are mutually consistent (e.g. the 3,129 mm-long AFL needing a 4.7 m right-angle-stack aisle, and the longer 2,942 mm APT needing 5.6 m, both track the expected Ast = truck length + load + clearance relationship), and every value validated cleanly against config/fields.json field names and allowed values (0 issues).

products.notes: All numeric values are the manufacturer's OWN printed METRIC column from the 2026/03 tear sheet (imperial/metric side by side), so no conversion error is possible: lift 60 in = 1,524 mm; payload 3,000 lb = 1,361 kg; L x W x H 123.2 x 43.4 x 96 in = 3129 x 1102 x 2438 mm; speed 6.7 mph = 3.0 m/s. min_total_height=2438 is the 'H' of the L x W x H triple (MEDIUM within an otherwise HIGH record -- the sheet does not label it as lowered-mast height, though that is the standard meaning of H in such a triple). min_aisle_width=4700 is the tear sheet's 'RIGHT ANGLE STACK 15 ft 6 in / 4.7 m'. IMPORTANT ALTERNATIVE: the same sheet also prints 'MINIMUM AISLE WIDTH AT MAX SPEED 9 ft / 2.7 m'. I chose 4.7 m because AP0 defines min_aisle_width as the working aisle; 2.7 m is only the corridor in which it can still travel at full speed and does NOT permit right-angle pallet handling. drive_type=Counterbalanced is stated by the product name and by the site ('counterbalanced forklift'). stacking_capability=true: 1,524 mm mast lift, explicitly lifts to/from conveyors, wrappers and risers. battery_type from 'Compatible with standard lead acid, lithium ion, and TPPL batteries' (TPPL = thin-plate pure lead, a lead-acid chemistry, so it folds into Lead-Acid). charge_time=120 is the UPPER bound of the published '1-2 hours charge time' range. autonomous_charging=true, but note it is listed as an ADD-ON accessory ('Autonomous charging with smart scheduling New!'); the base configuration uses manual opportunistic charging (the web page says 'Runs 24/7 using manual opportunistic charging'). barcode_readers=true from 'LPN Scanning -- scans pallet barcodes and sends updates to your WMS'. fleet_management_system=Proprietary (Pivotal Orchestration Engine). integration_capability limited to WMS -- the sheet says 'Remote tablet, WMS, and barcode scanning'; no REST/MQTT/OPC-UA/SAP claim exists, so nothing else was added. NOT SET: load_type (site only says 'a wide range of payloads and pallet types'; US pallet nomenclature does not map cleanly to the EUR/ISO vocabulary), mast_type, special_fork_option, fork_spread, stop/drop/pick accuracy, IP/temp/humidity/gradient -- none published. FORK LENGTH 42 in / 1,066 mm and WEIGHT (less battery) 4,700 lb / 2,132 kg are published but have no AP0 field. [FINALIZATION PASS] navigation_type=Natural Feature (SLAM) upgraded to fully confirmed via the official 'Pivotal Autonomous Navigation' page: Vecna builds 'a virtual map of your entire facility' and states 'Vecna AMRs are not limited to fixed routes and do not require any special infrastructure or markings to navigate'. This matches the AP0 mapping rule ('free navigation'/'marker-free'/'environment mapping' -> Natural Feature (SLAM)). autonomous_obstacle_bypass=true added on the same source: 'Free Space Reasoning(TM) allows AMRs to adjust their route and navigate around obstacles, without requiring assistance from workers', plus 'if congestion is too high on the prescribed route, Vecna's AMRs will pursue alternative available paths'. That is re-routing AROUND obstacles, exactly what the AP0 hint asks for, not merely stop-and-wait. This is a platform-level claim covering the whole fleet. fleet_control_architecture=Centralized added (MEDIUM): the Pivotal Orchestration Engine is a central cloud service that 'connects all routes and synchronizes with all vehicles in your fleet'; no swarm/on-board-negotiation claim exists. vda5050_compatible remains deliberately UNSET: a text scan of all seven Vecna sources collected (4 product pages, 4 tear sheets, navigation page, software-suite page, about page) returned ZERO occurrences of 'VDA' or '5050'. load_detection=['Barcode/DataMatrix'] added from the explicit 'LPN Scanning -- scans pallet barcodes and sends updates to your WMS' feature, which is how this truck identifies/verifies the pallet. Vecna also markets 'smart pallet detection' that 'scans the pickup area to identify the correct pallet ... and adjusts if anything is misaligned', but it never names the SENSOR modality, so 'Camera/Vision' and 'Laser/LiDAR profiling' were NOT added -- that would be guessing at the hardware.
